accepted.question_text: For the deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills equation, a fully nonlinear partial differential equation on holomorphic-side mirror-symmetry objects that is related by mirror symmetry to minimal Lagrangians, what are the dimensional reductions of the four-dimensional equation? In particular, after reducing along a Lagrangian fibration from four to two dimensions, can one understand the resulting local equations, the compact-surface case where the reduction becomes the Hitchin system, the punctured-surface case where new solutions may occur, and the analogues of the ADHM construction, Nahm-type equations, or monopoles where they are natural for the preferred complex structure of the deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills setting?

evidence.quote: Minimal Lagrangians and dHYM connections are related by mirror symmetry of Calabi-Yau manifolds and their existence is conjectured to be governed by a stability condition.
What are the dimensional reductions of 4-dimensional dHYM? The group derived the (local) equations for the dimensional reduction from 4 to 2 dimensions along a Lagrangian fibration.

accepted.question_text: Can the Thomas-Yau-Joyce conjecture be proved for the flat two-torus, including an explanation of why the Joyce program for proving it through Lagrangian mean curvature flow is not simply the usual curve-shortening-flow proof and how the proof reduces to the combinatorial task of identifying which curves in the two-torus are graded and unobstructed?

evidence.quote: Can one prove the Thomas-Yau-Joyce conjecture for the flat 2-torus? The group showed that the conjecture is true for the flat 2-torus

accepted.question_text: Do finite-time singularities occur for the deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills flow or for graphical Lagrangian mean curvature flow? The question includes cases beyond the Calabi-symmetric setting where the deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills flow reduces to a modified curve-shortening flow with no finite-time singularities, and it asks what analytic conditions, especially preservation of graphicality in the two-dimensional graphical Lagrangian mean curvature flow case, control the answer.
accepted.context_brief: Finite-time singularities in dHYM flow and graphical LMCF

evidence.quote: Are there finite-time singularities for the dHYM flow or graphical LMCF? The group studied the case of the dHYM flow in the Calabi-setting
key open questions in analysis of both the dHYM flow and graphical LMCF remain

accepted.question_text: What can be said about Lagrangian mean curvature flow and minimal Lagrangians in Kahler-Einstein manifolds with definite first Chern class, including the cases of complex projective space, negative first Chern class, mean curvature flow near minimal Lagrangians in negative Kahler-Einstein manifolds, and possible links from minimal Lagrangians to matrix factorizations and Landau-Ginzburg models through mirror symmetry?

evidence.quote: What can one say about LMCF and minimal Lagrangians in Kahler-Einstein manifolds with definite first Chern class? This group looked at LMCF for the case of CPn and for negative first Chern class.

accepted.question_text: What is the correct notion of the deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills equation for higher-rank bundles and for complexes of vector bundles? A proposed approach should account for examples motivated by the Euler sequence for the tangent bundle of complex projective two-space, by a Lagrangian multisection on the Landau-Ginzburg mirror of complex projective two-space, by Riemann-surface and quiver cases, by a corresponding Kempf-Ness functional, and by the relation between Lagrangian mean curvature flow for the mirror multisection and deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills theory.

evidence.quote: What is the correct notion of dHYM for higher rank bundles and complexes of vector bundles? The group used the Euler sequence for TCP2
the group considered LMCF for the Lagrangian multisection on the mirror of CP2 and its relation to dHYM.
